children: GoodVision AI (“GoodVision”), a developer of next-generation AI compute infrastructure purpose-built for inference, today announced that it will exhibit at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, taking place October 13–15, 2026, at Moscone West in San Francisco. The appearance follows the September 11 approval of GoodVision’s business combination with Calisa Acquisition Corp. (
), marking a new stage in the company’s development as it expands its AI inference infrastructure business.
GoodVision will exhibit at
Booth A3

, where it will showcase an integrated AI inference platform that combines intelligent workload routing, purpose-built compute infrastructure and cloud services. The platform is designed to help enterprises deploy and scale AI applications while balancing performance, cost, latency and data requirements.

TechCrunch Disrupt brings together more than 10,000 founders, investors, technology leaders and innovators to explore developments across artificial intelligence, infrastructure, robotics and other emerging technologies.

David Wang, CEO of GoodVision, said: “We are pleased to participate in TechCrunch Disrupt, where technology leaders, founders and investors gather to discuss the technologies shaping the future of business and innovation. As AI adoption accelerates, enterprises increasingly need infrastructure that can intelligently balance performance, cost, latency and data requirements. We look forward to connecting with founders, customers, investors and ecosystem partners to demonstrate GoodVision’s platform, and discuss how enterprises can move AI workloads into production at scale.”
At Booth A3, GoodVision will highlight three core components of its platform:
Smart Routing Engine
, which is designed to route AI inference requests to appropriate models and computing environments based on factors including cost, latency and data sensitivity;
AI Factories,
purpose-built computing infrastructure designed to support high-density AI inference workloads; and,
Cloud Services,
including cloud consulting, migration, optimization and managed services.

Together, these capabilities are designed to give enterprises a more flexible and efficient path to deploying, managing and scaling AI workloads across cloud, hybrid and dedicated computing environments.
Attendees interested in learning more about GoodVision AI and its AI infrastructure solutions are invited to visit the Company at
Booth A3
during TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. To arrange a meeting with the GoodVision team, contact
About GoodVision AI

GoodVision AI is building the global compute architecture for AI inference. Its platform pairs a real-time Smart Routing Engine with a network of purpose-built AI Factories to run AI efficiently atscale. The company is led by CEO David Wang. Learn more at goodvision.ai. GoodVision AI has entered into a BusinessCombination Agreement (the “BCA”) with Calisa Acquisition Corp, a Cayman Islands exempted company (

) whose business purpose is to effect a merger, capital stock exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or similar businesscombination with one or more businesses. The parties intend to consummate the transaction in the second half of 2026.
